open_points.subject: sandbox network-namespace invariant and failure handling
open_points.text: “the namespace's own loopback — up, as bubblewrap leaves it in a new network namespace, and reaching nothing outside the execution … this is a property of how the kernel starts bubblewrap, which the kernel does not inspect or verify at run time — the start check (rule 8) asks only that a probe execution succeeds”
open_points.question: What must happen if bubblewrap successfully runs the probe or an execution but the loopback is not up, another interface is present, or something outside the execution is reachable, given that the required environment invariant is unmet but no check, refusal, execution outcome or kernel-stop rule covers that case?
options: Trust a successful bubblewrap invocation and perform no further check
Have the startup probe verify the interface state and external isolation and refuse startup on mismatch
Verify every execution environment and classify or stop on mismatch
open_points.default_guess: Trust bubblewrap's namespace behavior and treat probe success as sufficient, because the change explicitly says the kernel does not inspect the property at run time.
